  "summary": "Keep pruned blocks in `m_blocks_unlinked` and re-add them during block index loading even when their block data is missing. Before updating a block's `nSequenceId` upon re-receiving transactions, erase it from `setBlockIndexCandidates` to prevent multiset order corruption. Update `CheckBlockIndex` assertions and enable out-of-chain block pruning in the `block_index_tree` fuzz target.",
  "problem": "When a node prunes a block whose parent's transactions have not yet been received, removing the block from `m_blocks_unlinked` prevents `m_chain_tx_count` from ever being computed if that missing parent arrives later (e.g., via `getblockfrompeer`). This puts the node into an inconsistent state, returns incorrect RPC data, and triggers assertion failures in `CheckBlockIndex`. Furthermore, re-downloading a pruned block mutates its `nSequenceId` while it resides in `setBlockIndexCandidates`, corrupting the set's sort order.",

result.summary: Keep pruned blocks in `m_blocks_unlinked` and re-add them during block index loading even when their block data is missing. Before updating a block's `nSequenceId` upon re-receiving transactions, erase it from `setBlockIndexCandidates` to prevent multiset order corruption. Update `CheckBlockIndex` assertions and enable out-of-chain block pruning in the `block_index_tree` fuzz target.
result.problem: When a node prunes a block whose parent's transactions have not yet been received, removing the block from `m_blocks_unlinked` prevents `m_chain_tx_count` from ever being computed if that missing parent arrives later (e.g., via `getblockfrompeer`). This puts the node into an inconsistent state, returns incorrect RPC data, and triggers assertion failures in `CheckBlockIndex`. Furthermore, re-downloading a pruned block mutates its `nSequenceId` while it resides in `setBlockIndexCandidates`, corrupting the set's sort order.
evidence: Closes issue #31512 ('validation: CheckBlockIndex can fail in combination with pruning') and issue #36021 ('validation: Assertion failed: ((pindexFirstNeverProcessed == nullptr || pindex == snap_base) == pindex->HaveNumChainTxs())')

Author notes the sequence ID corruption: 'nSequenceId is one of the sort keys of setBlockIndexCandidates, so changing it for a block that currently is in one of these sets corrupts their ordering, after which lookups for other entries can fail.'
Author notes the fuzzer impact: 'This was one of two reasons, the fuzz target block_index_tree couldn't cover pruning of blocks not in the main chain.'
result.card: This PR retains pruned blocks in `m_blocks_unlinked` across disk flushes and restarts, and removes candidates from `setBlockIndexCandidates` before modifying `nSequenceId` when block data is re-received. When parent blocks arrived out-of-order after a child block had been pruned, `m_chain_tx_count` failed to update, leading to internal state inconsistency and `CheckBlockIndex` assertion crashes (#31512, #36021). Mutating `nSequenceId` in-place also corrupted candidate set ordering. These fixes resolve the assertion failures and allow the `block_index_tree` fuzzer to prune out-of-chain blocks without crashing.
